mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has climbed from -19.7 to -9.0 over the last three weeks, indicating a steady return to commuting routines. This sustained recovery should continue feeding weekday retail footfall, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -19.7 to -9.0 across the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES remains flat or improving at or above -9.0.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has moved from -42.0 to -32.7 in the last two weeks. If this week-on-week improvement exceeds 5 points, it signals a meaningful unlock of commuter and shopper transit use that should translate into higher retail visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the following two weeks despite TRANSIT improving by more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are both recovering simultaneously (from -19.9/-42.0 to -9.0/-32.7). Their joint recovery compounds: commuters returning to offices also re-engage transit-adjacent retail corridors, producing a stronger lift in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show concurrent two-week improvement
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks is no larger than what a single-series (WORKPLACES-only) model would predict, indicating no interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has fallen from 7.4 to 4.0 over three weeks, consistent with relaxed stay-at-home policy pressure. Under a policy-easing regime, continued decline in RESIDENTIAL signals fewer compliance-driven confinements, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 4.0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over two weeks even as RESIDENTIAL continues to fall below 4.0, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward while RETAIL_REC still rises.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is highly volatile (5.0 to -18.6 to -11.1 to -15.6), suggesting outdoor recreation is substituting for indoor retail visits during warmer weeks. A sharp week-on-week rise in PARKS (>10 points) indicates diversion of discretionary trips away from retail destinations, lowering RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from -18.6 to -11.1 then back down to -15.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline following a PARKS jump of more than 10 points, or RETAIL_REC and PARKS move in the same direction repeatedly.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has steadily improved from -5.4 to -1.9, reflecting reduced precautionary stockpiling behavior and renewed comfort with in-person errands. This behavioral normalization is a leading indicator that spills over into general retail visits within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within one week despite GROCERY_PHARM continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT fails to improve beyond -30 for two consecutive weeks after its recent recovery, it signals that residual restrictions on movement (e.g., capacity limits, work-from-home mandates) remain binding, keeping shoppers away from retail precincts and suppressing RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT fails to improve beyond -30 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT currently at -32.7, not yet above -30
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over four weeks even though TRANSIT remains stalled below -30, invalidating the restriction-binding mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of falling RESIDENTIAL (less time at home) and rising WORKPLACES (more office attendance) jointly indicates a structural shift toward pre-pandemic routines. When both series move in tandem beyond their individual trends, the amplified reduction in home-bound behavior disproportionately boosts RETAIL_REC over four weeks via combined commute-and-errand trip chaining.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 7.4 to 4.0 while WORKPLACES rose from -19.9 to -9.0 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks is not greater than the sum of effects predicted by RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES independently, indicating no interaction-driven amplification.
